'''Dean Gunnar Hoffman''' (May 8, 1949 – November 11, 2022) was an American mathematician who worked primarily in [[graph theory]], [[Combinatorial design|design theory]], [[number theory]], and [[puzzle]]s.<ref name="MTU" />

== Early life and education ==
Hoffman was born on May 8, 1949. He was a [[backgammon]] player and would commonly play with students and collaborators. In 1970, he obtained his BA in mathematics from [[Union College]]. He then went on to be advised by [[David A. Klarner|David Klarner]] and Ron Mullin and obtain his PhD in mathematics from the [[University of Waterloo]] in 1976. <ref name="MTU">{{cite web |title=Dean Gunnar Hoffman |url=https://pages.mtu.edu/~kreher/ABOUTME/BICA/Hoffman.pdf |website=Michigan Technology University |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref>

== Career ==
He began working at Auburn University in 1977 until his death in 2022.<ref name="MTU" />

== Awards and honors ==
He has been awarded the Marie Kraska Award for the Excellence in Teaching in 2017 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=DMS congratulates Dr. Dean Hoffman |url=https://auburn.edu/cosam/news/articles/2022/04/dms_congratulates_dr._dean_hoffman.htm |website=Auburn University |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Dean Hoffman receives the 2017 Kraska Award |url=https://www.auburn.edu/cosam/news/articles/2017/03/dr.-dean-hoffman-receives-the-2017-kraska-award-.htm |website=Auburn University |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref>

In 2008, he was an invited speaker for the first Istanbul Design Theory and Combinatorics Conference which was held to celebrate the 70th birthday of [[Charles C. Lindner|Curt Lindner]], one of his collaborators.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mathematics and  Statistics - Department Highlights |url=https://www.auburn.edu/cosam/news/journey/documents/Journey2009.pdf |access-date=31 July 2025 |work=Journey |agency=The College of Science and Mathematics Auburn University |date=2009}}</ref> In 2014, Hoffman was invited to give the keynote address for the 8th Annual Troy MathFest at [[Troy University at Montgomery]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Hoffman to give keynote address at 8th annual MathFest |url=https://www.auburn.edu/academic/cosam/news/e-journey/archive/february/ |access-date=31 July 2025 |work=e-Journey |agency=Auburn University College of Sciences and Mathematics |date=February 2014}}</ref>

==Puzzles==
The [[Hoffman's packing puzzle]] is an [[Mechanical puzzle#Assembly puzzles|assembly puzzle]] which is named after Hoffman, who described it in 1978.<ref name=rausch>{{citation|url=https://johnrausch.com/PuzzleWorld/puz/hoffmans_packing_puzzle.htm|title=Put-Together – Hoffman's Packing Puzzle|work=Puzzle World|first=John|last=Rausch|accessdate=2019-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117012519/https://johnrausch.com/PuzzleWorld/puz/hoffmans_packing_puzzle.htm|archive-date=2019-11-17|url-status=live}}</ref> The puzzle consists of 27 identical rectangular [[cuboid]]s, each of whose edges have three different lengths. The goal of the puzzle is to assemble them all to fit within a cube whose edge length is the sum of the three lengths.<ref name=space>{{citation|title=A Mathematical Space Odyssey: Solid Geometry in the 21st Century|volume=50|series=Dolciani Mathematical Expositions|first1=Claudi|last1=Alsina|first2=Roger B.|last2=Nelsen|publisher=Mathematical Association of America|year=2015|isbn=9780883853580|contribution=Problem 3.10|page=63|contribution-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FEl2CgAAQBAJ&pg=PA63}}</ref>

== Death and legacy ==
He died on November 11, 2022.

His family created the Dr. Dean G. Hoffman Endowed Graduate Award in his honor.<ref name="Cosam Award">{{cite web |title=The Dr. Dean G. Hoffman Endowed Graduate Award has been established. |url=https://auburn.edu/cosam/news/articles/2023/06/the_dr._dean_g._hoffman_endowed_graduate_award_has_been_established.htm |website=Auburn University Cosam |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref>
